issue_context.title: Interested in adding RegNets to tf.keras.applications
issue_context.body:
**System information**.

TensorFlow version (you are using): 2.6.0
Are you willing to contribute it (Yes/No) : Yes

**Describe the feature and the current behavior/state**.

RegNets are used in self supervised vision works like SEER. They are also highly efficient and scalable architectures. I intend to train and incorporate RegNet-{X, Y, Z} in `tf.keras.applications`. I think having models that are fast, scalable and efficient be ready to use will greatly help the TF community.

**Will this change the current api? How?**
There will be new handles, namely `tf.keras.applications.RegNet{X, Y, Z}` in the API.

**Who will benefit from this feature?**
The entire TF Keras community.

**[Contributing](https://github.com/keras-team/keras/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)**

- Do you want to contribute a PR? (yes/no): yes

**Current Progress**

I have implemented the building blocks of RegNetY in [AdityaKane2001/regnety](https://github.com/AdityaKane2001/regnety). I have also trained 4 variants of RegNetY on ImageNet-1k and uploaded them to TFHub during Google Summer of Code 2021. 

[Published collection on TFHub](https://tfhub.dev/adityakane2001/collections/regnety/1)
[Repo link](https://github.com/AdityaKane2001/regnety)
[Project report link](https://adityakane2001.github.io/opensource/gsoc2021report)

/cc @sayakpaul
comments:
@fchollet I was one of the mentors of Aditya during GSoC and he did a phenomenal job. I wanted to provide more context and hence I am requesting Aditya to further clarify some points. 

> I think it will greatly help the TF-Keras community to get into self supervised vision.

@AdityaKane2001 just to be clear RegNets do not motivate the development of self-supervision drastically. It's because of their remarkable scaling capabilities, they were used in [SEER](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.01988) (to scale to billions of images). But it's important to note that ResNet50's been a pretty much standard baseline for most of the SSL stuff in vision that has happened over the last year (SimCLR, SwAV, MoCoV2, SimSiam, BYOL, Barlow Twins, etc.). 

I think the USPs of RegNet are the following:

* Smaller yet performs better. 
* Faster inference on commodity GPUs and mobile hardware.
* Scaling capabilities. 

These things do not necessarily only help self-supervision but also image recognition in general IMO. 

> I have also trained 4 variants of RegNetY on ImageNet

Make it explicitly clear that the models were trained on ImageNet-1k (there's ImageNet-21k too). Also, provide a link to your collection of the RegNetY models.

@fchollet 

If possible could you please take a look at this one? TIA

Hi there,

Yes, we'd welcome such a contribution. However, we have no availability to work on it, so you'd have to open a PR yourself (we will review the PR and guide you). Do you have an ImageNet checkpoint available for the model?

@fchollet @haifeng-jin @qlzh727 

Thanks for the reply.

To summarize, the objectives of my contribution are as follows:
- Add [RegNets](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2003.13678.pdf) to tf.keras.applications
- Train these models on ImageNet-1k or ImageNet-21k (please tell what would be preferable)

[Here](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/64411306/132623704-1b18097f-c7fb-4c24-8f81-603462742c81.png) is the basic structure of RegNetX in case you want to take a look.

This would require writing a lot of code and substantial training (there are 36 variants of them). Thus, it would be really helpful if you could give a concrete good-to-go so I can start working on it. This is also the reason I didn't directly open a PR.

@AdityaKane2001 cc. @rchao @fchollet 
It's a promising model and would be good to have it. However, does `RegNet` have enough citations to be part of the `keras` application? If I'm not mistaken it currently has around 16 citations which is less than 50 citations threshold.

I am not sure which citation stats you referred to @innat but it definitely seems wrong:

![Screenshot 2021-09-18 at 8 42 21 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22957388/133893558-f3ba9ce2-7ee5-45b5-af01-03d0629b1a42.png)

![Screenshot 2021-09-18 at 8 41 47 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22957388/133893561-302cb14d-bfcc-4b11-90af-34122fb61c06.png)
@haifeng-jin could you provide an update on this? Should we start working on the PR?
@fchollet would be the best person to make the decision here.

@haifeng-jin 

Yes, he has given the green light. We are now working on the PR : #15419
